common_prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: one original architecture and environment design board for the first-person mystery game 《错日证词》 (Wrong Date Testimony), January 1931 in fictional Qingchuan town, no real country assigned.
Primary request: create a rich, polished landscape concept sheet for ONE vehicle repair shop. This is one of five alternatives; show one coherent design only.
Composition: refined cream editorial margins, a small exact Chinese title at top. Upper half: large attractive exterior three-quarter establishing view showing the entire building and its yard without clipping. Lower-left: immersive human-eye-height workshop interior. Lower-right: legible roof-removed axonometric showing the same building, same openings, circulation and usable room arrangement. A narrow bottom strip shows five period props from this workshop. All views must agree with each other as architectural concepts. Labels only “外观”, “维修间”, “空间示意”, “道具”; no prose or invented dimensions.
Game art: believable carefully modeled 3D environment concept render with restrained stylization, readable forms, weathered handmade materials, cinematic atmospheric lighting, rich detail without photoreal estate advertisement or toy-like blocks. Palette stays compatible with the game's subdued grey-green, blue-violet shadows, cream plaster, aged timber, patinated iron and warm amber lamps. Quiet winter overcast dusk, warm readable interiors, a little wet paving only for visual atmosphere.
Shared functions: a small customer reception counter accessible directly from the street, a public-side writing desk with closed customer ledger and loose work-order papers, a genuine repair hall large enough for one 1930-era compact working vehicle, an adjacent motorcycle work position, sturdy workbench with bench vise and period tools, parts shelves, a small oil and rag store, a separated modest back office, and a rear delivery yard. Keep a clear human walking route from the public counter to the workshop edge and through to the rear yard. Machinery and vehicles must not block circulation. Modest town business scaled to an approximately 18m-wide street parcel with a deep rear yard, not a gigantic factory. This is a proposed building design, not a fixed final construction drawing.
Story constraints: the owner is the wife's lover, but do NOT depict a murder, threatening character, crime board, blood, secret evidence, or a villain sign. The local shop is a place to inspect tools and records. His historical alibi comes from records and witness copies from a different-city workshop: don't invent an alibi scene or assert he worked here that evening. All paper text is blank or indecipherable neutral strokes; no invented dates, names, clue answers, narrative labels or timelines. No people required.
Period props: hand tools, spanners, an oily cloth, wood-and-metal parts drawers, a paper work-order folder, a manual chain hoist or jack if called for. One unbranded 1920s/early-1930s compact vehicle and one period motorcycle maximum. No modern automobile, modern motorcycle, hydraulic two-post car lift, computers, CCTV, plastic bins, neon, fluorescent strips, modern fire exit sign, logos, flags, national symbols, digital clock, shiny epoxy floor, wreckage ruin or palace. No modern warning graphics.
Architecture-specific direction and exact title follow.

schemes.title: A｜砖木街铺
schemes.direction:
Exact header: “A · 砖木街铺”.
A: an intimate established town street workshop, 18m-wide two-storey red-brown brick front house and single-storey L-shaped rear wing around a hard-surfaced yard. Charcoal pitched slate roof, cream-painted window lintels, dark green timber folding garage door on one side, glazed oak customer entrance on the other, aged timber fascia bearing only “修车铺”. Upper floor has real small office/break rooms reached by an actual side staircase shown in the cutaway; upper windows correspond to usable rooms, not a fake upper facade. Ground workshop behind the folding doors, reception and writing counter beside it facing street, back wing tool store. One small boxy dark olive 1930 sedan in the bay with its hood open, motorcycle beside the rear bench. Honey-colored lamps, brick pillars, wood tool drawers and worn cement floor. A domestic neighborhood business, compact urban silhouette and warm craft character.

schemes.title: B｜车马院工坊
schemes.direction:
Exact header: “B · 车马院工坊”.
B: a low timber-and-cream-masonry repair courtyard adapted from a carriage yard. Three one-storey wings form a U around an open working court, southern street entrance through a broad timber gateway in a low wall, rear left reception room with glazed window onto courtyard, covered repair stalls in the back wing, parts store in one side wing. Dark moss-painted vertical timber boarding, pale plaster lower walls, warm terracotta-grey hipped tiles, deep eaves, plain old carriage lamps. No upper floor, no brick street facade, no sawtooth roof. The exterior high three-quarter view clearly reveals an OPEN courtyard and the real roofs of three wings; show a broad gateway allowing a compact vintage utility vehicle to enter without a steps barrier. Workshop interior looks through large open timber bay doors to the same court. One small period utility pickup at the back covered stall, one motorcycle on a low wooden service stand, manual overhead chain block. Sheltered pedestrian perimeter remains separate from vehicle path. Quiet practical yard, winter bare tree outside the work zone, restrained irregular texture.

schemes.title: C｜奶白几何车房
schemes.direction:
Exact header: “C · 奶白几何车房”.
C: a crisp 1931 small-town early-modern garage, one-storey ivory plaster frontage with stepped parapet and modest geometric pilasters, green-grey framed tall rectangular glazing, recessed jade-green double vehicle doors, compact angular customer reception projecting at one side, gently pitched roof hidden behind parapet with a real rear clerestory, narrow rear parts wing and walled yard. No tower, no grand palace, no glass curtain wall, no neon, no classical colonnade. Restrained Art Deco period geometry, charcoal concrete skirting, old brass door pull and opal glass pendant. Wide luminous repair room with high horizontal clerestory windows, plain cream plaster and teak-green counter; removable floorboard covers over a shallow inspection trench with safe access and an uninterrupted adjacent walking path. One unbranded small black 1930 touring car, bicycle-size period motorcycle beside tool bench. Clean but used, modestly prosperous independent proprietor, softened dust and oil wear, not a modern car dealership. Entire building must look feasible at 17m facade width.

schemes.title: D｜天窗铁架工坊
schemes.direction:
Exact header: “D · 天窗铁架工坊”.
D: a compact industrial repair hall with a distinctive TWO-tooth sawtooth north-light roof, weathered charcoal-brown brick, dark riveted iron and steel window frames, sloped grey zinc roof surfaces and glazed vertical roof lights, one single-storey low customer/ledger office projecting in front at the right, broad charcoal timber sliding vehicle door at left, a narrow rear supply yard with spare parts crates. No residential upper floor, no tiled hipped roof, no semicircular stone arches, no huge factory chimney. The hall is truly single-storey and light pours down from the same two sawtooth roof windows shown outside and in cutaway. Trussed beams carry a small manual chain hoist; visible thin iron structure without modern gantry equipment. One compact period commercial van with hood open, a motorcycle repair bench, iron shelving, used metal parts, old stamped drawers, amber shaded work lamps. Public ledger desk separated from dirty work by a glazed timber partition. Strong structural silhouette, everyday modest industrial precision, atmospheric but maintained, not abandoned horror.

schemes.title: E｜旧石仓修车院
schemes.direction:
Exact header: “E · 旧石仓修车院”.
E: a repair shop converted from an old stone storage barn. A tall single-volume grey-buff roughstone hall with THREE narrow transverse timber gables along its length and aged slate roofs, a broad low segmental-arch stone vehicle doorway, dark walnut split folding doors, tall narrow plain metal-framed windows with heavy stone reveals. A low cream-plaster customer office adjoins the street end on one side, a timber lean-to parts shed joins at the back and encloses a modest rear yard. No symmetrical two-storey civic building, no courtyard U wings, no sawtooth industrial roof, no Art Deco parapet. Inside, exposed heavy old timber roof trusses and rough stone walls above a practical worn flagstone/cement work floor, a real small accessible storage loft only above the back tool store with an actual straight stair in the cutaway. One deep burgundy small 1930 automobile beneath a manual timber-supported chain hoist, motorcycle near the side-wall workbench; warm copper-shaded lamps, pale limewashed arch interior, wooden pigeonhole shelves, a reception desk at the attached office looking into the hall. Most secluded old-world, solid weathered craft atmosphere, still an active maintained workshop.

revisions.prompt: Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit target: the attached A · 砖木街铺 concept board. Make ONLY the large upper exterior panel camera pull back slightly, about 15%, and reframe downward so the ENTIRE main two-storey building and its charcoal pitched roof are visible, including ridge and chimney tops with a small clear sky margin. The current top border clips the upper roof; fix that cropping. Keep the design of the red-brown brick street workshop, all doors and windows, repaired 1930 vehicle, motorcycle, single-storey L rear wing, yard and lighting. Keep the board's panel rectangles and typography EXACTLY unchanged, exact title “A · 砖木街铺”. Preserve the lower interior, lower cutaway, and bottom prop strip exactly; do not redesign, add rooms or change any story element. Refined game environment concept art, same palette, materials and resolution. No extra panels or text.
